topic: Geological Genesis of Coal from Ancient Swamp Flora
questionText:
Arrange the stages of geological coalification over hundreds of millions of years under heat and pressure:
(I) Dense ancient swamp forests and giant lycophyte ferns die, accumulating in stagnant, oxygen-poor water basins
(II) Partial microbial decomposition in anaerobic mire forms spongy, high-moisture 'Peat'
(III) Burial beneath thousands of meters of sedimentary rock compresses peat into brown, soft 'Lignite'
(IV) Intense tectonic thermal maturation and overburden pressure convert lignite into hard 'Bituminous' and finally metamorphic 'Anthracite' coal

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Geological Genesis of Coal from Ancient Swamp Flora.

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Environmental and Natural Resource Economics (Geological Genesis of Coal from Ancient Swamp Flora):
I -> II -> III -> IV

Detailed Analysis:
Coal formation: swamp accumulation, anaerobic peat formation, sedimentary compression into lignite, and thermal maturation into bituminous/anthracite.
Hence, Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

options.text: Pollution will always increase exponentially until all parties go bankrupt

options.text: Private bargaining between the polluter and affected parties will lead to an economically efficient allocation of resources, regardless of who initially holds the property rights

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

Private bargaining between the polluter and affected parties will lead to an economically efficient allocation of resources, regardless of who initially holds the property rights

Coase demonstrated that with zero transaction costs and clear property rights, voluntary bargaining internalizes externalities efficiently without direct regulatory taxation.
Hence, Option A is correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
